Hi Ellen —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is an itemized acceptance/evidence definition you can paste into the SOW. I kept the wording operational so Legal can reference the telemetry types rather than implementation. If you want, we can convert to a table for the SOW appendix.

1) Definitions
- Availability (Success Rate): Percentage of customer requests that return a 2xx status (or equivalent success marker) within the configured request timeout. Failed requests include 5xx responses, network errors, timeouts, and explicit model-service-level errors (generation aborted).
- Latency: Server-side end-to-end processing time measured from request receipt to final token emit (or response close). Reported percentiles: p50, p95, p99.

2) Measurement window & sampling
- Primary measurement window: Monthly calendar window (00:00 UTC on day 1 to 23:59:59 UTC on final day).
- Sampling cadence: Per-request evaluation. For high-throughput customers we aggregate by 1-minute buckets internally and compute exact percentiles from bucketed histograms to control cardinality.
- Synthetic probes: Treated as a separate telemetry stream but included in the published probe-derived availability figure. Final availability used for crediting = weighted composite: 75% customer-traffic success rate + 25% synthetic-probe success rate by default. Weighting can be adjusted for Dedicated contracts (default becomes 100% customer-traffic).

3) Attribution & regional weighting
- Multi-region customers: availability is computed per-region and then weighted by observed customer traffic to the account for the monthly window. If region-specific probes indicate an isolated regional degradation, crediting is region-scoped and applied proportionally to traffic affected.

4) Incident windows, burst immunity, and partial-day events
- Incident windowing: an incident is defined as a contiguous period where measured availability for affected endpoints drops below the threshold. Small transient drops under 2 minutes are treated as transient and excluded from crediting calculation (burst immunity).
- Overlapping incidents are de-duplicated by unioning time ranges; credits are calculated on the unioned impact window to avoid double crediting.

5) Service credit formula
- Baseline SLO target (example): 99.90% availability for Hosted API; 99.95% for Dedicated capacity if purchased.
- ObservedAvailability = (weighted success rate for the monthly window).
- RawCredit = max(0, (SLO_target - ObservedAvailability) / SLO_target)
- MonthlyServiceCredit = RawCredit * MonthlyRecurringFees
- Credit Cap: Hosted API standard cap = 10% of MonthlyRecurringFees; Dedicated cap = 100% of MonthlyRecurringFees (only for customers with reserved capacity contracts).
- Partial-day / pro-rata: Credits are calculated on the monthly window; a 3-hour outage is reflected in ObservedAvailability and pro-rated via the formula above rather than a separate daily proration.

6) Evidence package required to validate a credit claim
- Time-windowed CSV export with per-minute aggregated metrics (success_count, total_count, latency_histogram bins), signed by Redwood engineering with a timestamp and tracing id mapping.
- Synthetic probe logs for the window (probe id, timestamp, status, region).
- Engine trace snippets for a sample of failed requests (redacted PII) showing request id, model variant, node id, and failure code.
- Dashboard snapshot (PDF) with p99 latency trend and availability graph for the month.
- Attestation: a short statement from Redwood reliability engineering asserting the observed calculation and any adjustments made during post-incident reconciliation.

7) Dispute window and SLAs for evidence submission
- Customers have 30 days from invoice issuance to open a credit request with the required evidence. Redwood will respond within 10 business days with a preliminary assessment and produce full reconciliation within 30 business days.

8) Exceptions & blackout windows
- Scheduled maintenance that is communicated 72+ hours in advance is excluded from crediting. Emergency maintenance may be excluded if documented and agreed with the customer.

Attachments: Redwood-SLO-Evidence-Spec-v1.pdf (detailed field-level schema for the CSV exports)

If that looks good I can flag specific clauses for Legal. Also note we can alter the probe weighting if Solara prefers 90/10 (customer/probe) or to go 100% customer-traffic for Dedicated. Happy to walk through the math examples on a quick call.

Lauren — thank you, this is exactly the level of detail we need. A couple quick clarifications before I pass to Legal:

- The 2-minute burst immunity makes sense; can you confirm the rationale and whether that is configurable per customer?
- For the composite weighting: can you give a short numeric example for a month where customer-traffic availability = 99.75% and probes = 99.2% using the default 75/25 weighting? I want to show the math to our finance folks.
- If we are contracted for multi-region coverage and we see an isolated regional drop that impacted 8% of our traffic, do you apply the credit to the whole invoice or only to the region-proportioned portion?

Also, Ben asked whether Hosted customers can get a higher credit cap for committed spend tiers — is that something Redwood will consider (Ben will follow up with numbers).

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>

Subject: Internal: Solara SLO clarifications — Hosted credit cap exception?

Lauren / Marissa — quick internal note after Ellen's follow-up:

- Answer the numeric example inline: With customer-traffic = 99.75% and probes = 99.20%, composite = 0.75*99.75 + 0.25*99.20 = 99.59% approx. If our Hosted target is 99.90%, RawCredit = (99.90 - 99.59) / 99.90 = 0.31 / 99.90 = 0.003103 => MonthlyServiceCredit = 0.3103% of MonthlyRecurringFees.
- For isolated regional drops that affect X% of traffic, we currently apply region-weighted crediting (i.e., we only credit proportionally to affected traffic). This is already in the SOW wording but call it out to Legal.
- Ben is asking whether we can raise Hosted credit cap to 20% for Solara if they commit to a 12-month prepay at a qualifying tier. I think we can approve this commercial exception but must loop Legal for contract language and Finance for ARR/commitment verification.

Action: Lauren, please ACK this in the thread to Ellen and propose a short call for Friday to finalize. Marissa, can you start a redline template for a Hosted exception (20% cap) and tag Legal (we'll add Ben from Solara).
